headline: G7 finance leaders plan to hold exercises on AI cyberattacks
body: G7 finance leaders agreed to hold tabletop exercises on AI cyber attacks, Japanese finance minister Satsuki Katayama said. The simulations will test how finance authorities respond to AI-driven cyberattacks, and private financial institutions could take part, depending on the nature of the simulations.
note: The IMF had warned that an AI-enabled attack on a critical service could undermine confidence, and the results will be used to revise manuals.

evidence.text: Finance leaders of the G7 grouping agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, Japanese finance minister Satsuki Katayama said, as policymakers increasingly seek to co-ordinate responses to growing cybersecurity risks.
The agreement comes after the International Monetary Fund (IMF) warned this week that confidence could be undermined by an AI-enabled cyberattack on a critical service of a financial institution.

The plan will feature simulations evolved by G7 finance authorities to test how they can respond to AI-driven cyberattacks, said a Japanese finance ministry official who attended the finance leaders’ meeting.
The results will test the effectiveness of existing protocols and be used to revise manuals to better tackle such incidents, the official told reporters.
The exercises by G7 finance ministries and central banks could include private financial institutions depending on the nature of simulations, the official added.
